hook.line: Altamira keeps raising its offer, and Tomás keeps saying no, even though the café is losing money. To admit a fact and then act against it, Spanish has a small set of linking phrases, and you will hear them in every news report.
hook.es: A pesar de que el café pierde plata, Tomás no quiere vender.
hook.en: Despite the fact that the café is losing money, Tomás doesn't want to sell.

examples.es: A pesar de la lluvia, vinieron.
A pesar de que el café pierde plata, Tomás no quiere vender.
examples.en: Despite the fact that the café is losing money, Tomás doesn't want to sell.

examples.es: Es caro; sin embargo, vale la pena.
examples.en: It's expensive; however, it's worth it.

examples.es: Hernando tiene setenta años. Aun así, camina todos los días.
examples.en: Hernando is seventy. Even so, he walks every day.

examples.es: Estudié mucho. Aun así, no pasé el examen.
examples.en: I studied a lot. Even so, I didn't pass the exam.

examples.es: Salimos a pesar de que llueve.
examples.en: We're going out even though it's raining.

examples.es: A pesar de todo, Tomás se queda en el café.
examples.en: Despite everything, Tomás is staying at the café.

rule:
You already know *aunque*. These phrases do the same job, with different grammar.

*A pesar de* + a noun: *A pesar de la lluvia, vinieron.*
*A pesar de que* + a full clause: *A pesar de que llueve, salimos.* Keep the *de*, and keep the *que* before a verb.

*Sin embargo* and *aun así* start a new sentence (or follow a semicolon). They answer what was just said: *Es caro; sin embargo, vale la pena.* *Aun así* adds a feeling of stubbornness: even so, I'm doing it.

Never add *pero* next to any of them. Each one already carries the "but".

The verb after *a pesar de que* is the plain verb you already know, because you are stating a fact.
smallPrint: Teachers call these concessive connectors. They concede a fact, then carry on against it. *Sin embargo* is a little more formal than *aun así*.

readAndPick.es: A pesar de la lluvia, vinieron.
options: They came because of the rain.
They came despite the rain.
They didn't come because of the rain.

readAndPick.es: Es caro; sin embargo, vale la pena.
options: It's expensive, so it's not worth it.
It's cheap, so it's worth it.
It's expensive, but it's worth it.
Even so, I'm not signing.
That's why I'm not signing.
I'm signing anyway.

readAndPick.es: A pesar de que el café pierde plata, Tomás no quiere vender.
options: Because the café loses money, Tomás wants to sell.
The café loses money, but Tomás doesn't want to sell.
Tomás doesn't want to sell because the café loses money.

readAndPick.es: Hernando tiene setenta años. Aun así, camina todos los días.
options: Hernando is seventy, so he walks every day.
Hernando is seventy and he doesn't walk any more.
Hernando is seventy, but he still walks every day.

readAndPick.es: Estudié mucho. Aun así, no pasé el examen.
options: I studied a lot and still didn't pass the exam.
I studied a lot, so I passed the exam.
I didn't study, so I didn't pass the exam.

readAndPick.es: Salimos a pesar de que llueve.
options: We stay in because it's raining.
We go out even though it's raining.
We go out because it's raining.

readAndPick.es: Hace frío. Sin embargo, Tomás abre la ventana.
options: It's cold, so Tomás opens the window.
It's cold, and Tomás closes the window.
It's cold, but Tomás opens the window anyway.

readAndPick.es: A pesar de todo, Tomás se queda en el café.
options: Despite everything, Tomás stays at the café.
Because of everything, Tomás leaves the café.
Thanks to everything, Tomás stays at the café.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *a pesar de* or *por*, and type the whole sentence: *___ la lluvia, vinieron.* (They came despite the rain.)
yourTurn.answer: A pesar de la lluvia, vinieron.
yourTurn.why: The rain should have stopped them and didn't: *a pesar de*.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *sin embargo* or *por eso*, and type the whole sentence: *Es caro; ___, vale la pena.* (It's expensive; however, it's worth it.)
yourTurn.answer: Es caro; sin embargo, vale la pena.
accept: Es caro. Sin embargo, vale la pena.
yourTurn.why: "However" turns against what came before: *sin embargo*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: Despite the rain, we arrived on time. (we)
yourTurn.answer: A pesar de la lluvia, llegamos a tiempo.
accept: Llegamos a tiempo a pesar de la lluvia.
yourTurn.why: *A pesar de* plus a noun, then what happened anyway.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: Even so, I'm not signing. (I)
yourTurn.why: *Aun así* answers what was just said: even so.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: Despite the fact that Tomás is tired, he's working.
yourTurn.answer: A pesar de que Tomás está cansado, trabaja.
accept: Tomás trabaja a pesar de que está cansado.
A pesar de que Tomás está cansado, está trabajando.
yourTurn.why: Before a verb, *a pesar de* needs *que*.

yourTurn.prompt: Join the two sentences with *aun así*: *Estudié mucho. No pasé el examen.* (I studied a lot. I didn't pass the exam.)
yourTurn.answer: Estudié mucho. Aun así, no pasé el examen.
yourTurn.why: *Aun así* sits at the start of the second sentence and carries the "but".

yourTurn.prompt: Say the same thing with *a pesar de que*: *Salimos aunque llueve.* (We're going out even though it's raining.)
yourTurn.answer: Salimos a pesar de que llueve.
accept: A pesar de que llueve, salimos.
yourTurn.why: *A pesar de que* and *aunque* both introduce a fact that didn't stop you.

pitfalls.right: A pesar de la lluvia, vinieron.
pitfalls.why: Almost. The *de* is part of the phrase, so it never drops out.

pitfalls.right: A pesar de que llueve, salimos.
pitfalls.why: Almost. Before a verb you need *que*: *a pesar de que* + verb.

pitfalls.wrong: Es caro, pero sin embargo vale la pena.
pitfalls.right: Es caro; sin embargo, vale la pena.
pitfalls.why: *Sin embargo* already means "but", so adding *pero* says it twice.

pitfalls.wrong: A pesar de que el café pierde plata, pero Tomás no quiere vender.
pitfalls.right: A pesar de que el café pierde plata, Tomás no quiere vender.
pitfalls.why: The opening phrase already carries the contrast, so there is no *pero* in the second half.

personal: Tell us something you do *a pesar de* a difficulty, or finish this: *Estoy cansado, pero aun así…* Use *a pesar de*, *sin embargo* or *aun así* once.
